headline: Ottawa Prints the Matching Tariff List
deck: Finance Canada said counter-tariffs of 15, 25 and 50 percent will apply to products covering $27.6 billion of U.S. imports from 12:01 a.m. on 8 September. Steel and aluminum already under a 25 percent counter-tariff move to 50 percent. The 25 August artifact is a news-release list. No Gazette Part II order had printed by the freeze.
body: Finance Canada published the missing instrument on 25 August: a product list for counter-tariffs covering $27.6 billion in imports from the United States [E1][E2]. The rates are 15, 25 and 50 percent, matching the corresponding U.S. Section 338 and 232 rates on each product [E1]. The measures take effect at 12:01 a.m. on 8 September 2026 and do not apply to goods in transit that day [E2]. 12:01 a.m. EDT is 04:01 UTC [E2].

Steel and aluminum products that were previously only subject to a 25 percent counter-tariff move to 50 percent, along with furniture and clothing in that band [E1]. The 25 percent band includes appliances, dairy such as cheese, fish and seafood, and certain steel and aluminum derivative products [E1]. The complete-list page is the line-item ledger [E3]. Reuters rendered the same envelope as about US$20 billion; the official figure is Canadian dollars [E1].

The same announcement carries a $7.5 billion package of new and enhanced support measures [E1]. What did not print by the freeze is a Canada Gazette Part II order for the September 8 measures [E3]. Administration is described through CBSA customs notices [E3]. The 22 August U.S. 50 percent action on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods is the one-sentence prior [E1]. Monday’s icebreaker award is a separate NSS contract.
Whether the 25 August schedule is actually in force at 04:01 UTC on 8 September is already on the Tape [E1][E2]. A list is not yet a customs liability.
